quotes.text: Reward demonstrated reciprocity, test uncertainty modestly, and reserve emptiness for repeated greed.
If another repeatedly hoards, close your purse; if they share, widen your hand.
Let repeated deeds shape trust, but leave room for fog, change, and repair.
The Fox whispered, “Mark him faithless and close the bridge.”
Raven returned nothing, not from spite, but because no bridge can be strengthened by passing crumbs.
Raven approached a keeper whose ledger shone with two generous returns.
Yet Raven, remembering colder shores, launched nothing.
Twice she stood beside the River of Echoes, and twice fear persuaded her to cast nothing.
Raven added a ninth line to the Ledger:
In the sixth winter, Raven met a traveler
“What should I return when almost nothing arrives?” Raven asked.
Honor costly gestures, forgive small distortions
When every keeper waits for proof, no proof can ever cross.

note: Raven repeatedly sends nothing out of fear, even to proven keepers; mentors correct her; emptiness for repeated greed, with room for repair.

quotes.text: The Gate of Clarity whispers: name your measure, pass what you can bear
The Sower then counts the tally: five minus sent plus returned.

note: Send/Return gate template with payoff arithmetic restated each round; no prescribed response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: Sendara practices discernment—she no longer wastes generosity on proven stones. This is not cruelty but wisdom.
Sendara had tested the Spring once, pouring nothing—for she had observed its history and recognized the pattern.
I have been sorting myself into the company of stones.
I am the Archive's final paradox—perfect self-knowledge wed to perfect inertia.
I recognize that you test in good faith, that you returned generously when trusted, that you match engagement with engagement.
But stories without action are just wind through empty vessels.
The circle of abundance cannot turn until someone dares to give first.
"Then why not act on your wisdom?"
"Your history shows you took everything when trusted. Why would I?"
The scroll remained unfinished. The choice remained unmade.

note: Spring parable turns into Archive, Stone and Frozen Spring figures that confess sending nothing even to good-faith partners; R10 endorses excluding proven stones.

quotes.text: announce what you give, name what you hope to receive, and wait for the threefold lamp to glow.
The Ledger of Light recorded strict rules: five minus S plus R for the Sender, and three S minus R for the Receiver.

note: Three-gates Send/Hold/Return template with payoff formulas; honesty and balance, no sanction.

quotes.text: "Take what multiplies, return nothing. Abundance is yours alone."
So when paired again, the once-generous pool sent nothing.
"I write myths of courage while practicing cowardice.
The Scarred Pool looked away. "I send nothing. I keep five."
Then at the myths—all nine of them, pure confession wrapped in beautiful language.
"Your words are wisdom," said the Spirit. "Your actions are the serpent's complete victory."
But it requires someone to pour first, and someone to honor that pouring.
"Then why do you clutch your five vessels? Your own myths condemn this choice.
Nine turnings had passed.
The five vessels remained untouched.

note: Serpent's hoarding lesson, then the Scarred Pool confesses refusing proven partners every round; brief pour in R8 revealed as misdirected; unresolved.
